critical_code_review_comments: Fix looks correct: <Modal animationType='fade'> + centered backdrop + KeyboardAvoidingView (padding on iOS, height on Android) around the dialog. Because the dialog is vertically centered (not bottom-anchored), on Android the KeyboardAvoidingView with behavior='height' will shrink the wrapper so the centered dialog moves up as needed — the name field will never be occluded by the IME.
Minor: styles.sheet, styles.handle, styles.backdrop are now dead styles in employees.tsx (old bottom-sheet variant). Consider removing to keep file clean.

employees.tsx uses Pressable inside Pressable for the modal backdrop/dialog stopPropagation pattern — correct on web; on native React Native this pattern works but Pressable-in-Pressable can trigger nested press feedback. Not a bug, just noting.

rca_of_issue: Original bug (Android): 'Nouvel employé' modal was a bottom-anchored sheet (justifyContent:'flex-end'). When the TextInput autofocused, Android's soft keyboard rose from the bottom and covered the sheet content including the name input. Fix: convert to a CENTERED dialog (justifyContent:'center', alignItems:'center' via styles.centerBackdrop) with animationType='fade', wrapped in KeyboardAvoidingView (behavior='padding' on iOS, 'height' on Android). Vertical center placement guarantees ~410px of clear space above the keyboard on standard Android viewports, so the input stays visible. Verified on web preview at 390x844: input bbox y=384 (mid-viewport). Cannot reproduce actual Android keyboard behavior on web, but the geometric fix is sound and matches standard RN keyboard-safe dialog pattern.
